summary_plain: The Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II (SAFFIRE-II) investigated large-scale fire growth and material flammability limits in microgravity using an expendable Cygnus cargo vehicle after it departed the International Space Station. By burning multiple material samples in a controlled flow duct, the experiment tested how reduced gravity affects flame spread and compared the results to standard terrestrial flammability tests. Understanding these fire behaviors is critical to improving fire safety and material selection for future crewed spacecraft.
summary_expert: SAFFIRE-II was conducted inside an experiment module measuring approximately 53- by 90- by 133-cm installed on an Orbital Science's Cygnus resupply vehicle. The hardware featured a flow duct containing a sample card with 9 samples, each measuring 5 cm x 29 cm, including SIBAL, silicone, structure PMMA, flat PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex. Depending on the material, tests were performed at air flow velocities of either 20 or 30 cm/s in concurrent or opposed configurations. Data collection instruments included two video cameras, thermocouples for temperature measurements, two radiometers for flame radiation, solid state sensors for pressure, CO2, and O2 mole fractions, and two anemometers to track flow velocity. The documents provided describe the objectives and design only.

key_findings.text: The Saffire-II sample card contains 9 samples, each 5 cm x 29 cm, comprising materials such as SIBAL, silicone, structure PMMA, flat PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex.
Depending on the sample material, tests on Saffire-II were conducted at an air flow velocity of either 20 or 30 cm/s, with the flow being either concurrent or opposed.
The experiment module consists of a flow duct and an adjacent avionics bay, with dimensions of approximately 53- by 90- by 133-cm.
